lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Job Readiness: Applications, Resumes, and Interviews
lessonRef.title: Independent application: interview preparation and follow-up

objective: Learners build a logistics checklist for arriving prepared to a real interview and draft a short, specific thank-you follow-up message referencing something from the practice interview, without sending it, so they understand both sides of the interview process.
scenario: Building on the practice interview from the previous lesson, the learner creates a short logistics checklist (what to bring, how to confirm timing, what questions to ask the interviewer) and drafts a thank-you follow-up message that references one specific thing discussed, kept as a draft only.
safetyNotes: This draft follow-up message is never sent as part of the lesson.
materials: notes from the previous lesson's practice interview

tasks.directions: List everything you would need to have ready before a real interview (what to bring, how to confirm the time, how you'd get there).

prompts.text: List at least four items or steps you'd need ready before a real interview.

tasks.directions: Turn your list into a short, usable logistics checklist, and add two genuine questions you would ask the interviewer.

prompts.text: My checklist includes confirming the time and place ahead of the interview.
Write two genuine questions you would ask the interviewer, and explain why each one is useful to you, not just filler.

tasks.directions: Draft a short thank-you follow-up message referencing one specific thing from your practice interview.

prompts.text: Draft a three-to-four sentence thank-you message that references one specific thing discussed in the practice interview, not a generic 'thanks for your time.'

tasks.directions: Reflect on why the follow-up matters.

prompts.text: Explain in your own words what a specific follow-up message shows an interviewer that a generic one doesn't.

remediation: If a learner's questions for the interviewer are generic ('what's it like working here') or their follow-up message is a bare 'thanks,' reteach by requiring both to reference one concrete detail from the actual practice interview notes before they count as complete.
extension: Have the learner draft a second follow-up message for a scenario where the interview went poorly in one specific way, and explain how the message would need to differ.
